observations: Used transmission sitting on a wooden floor in a workshop or garage.
The unit is labeled 'P105' and 'AUSTIN' in white paint on the casing.
A 'Goodman Transmission' brand sticker is visible on the side of the casing in photo 1.
The casing shows significant surface rust and dirt, suggesting it is used.
The output shaft is visible at the front of the unit.
The seller's text mentions 'American drive toks standard' and 'We have every parts for Chevrolet'.
Watermarks 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'GEARUP INC.' are present on all images.

claims.evidence: The 'P105' code is typical for a 4-speed automatic, but it does not confirm compatibility with a Chevrolet Express.

claims.claim: We have every parts for Chevrolet
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The transmission may not be compatible with the Chevrolet Express model.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's identification plate (usually on the side or back of the casing).

risks.risk: Internal mechanical damage or leaks may exist despite the exterior appearance.
risks.proof: A video of the unit being shifted through all gears.

risks.risk: The output shaft may be cracked or seized.
risks.proof: A video showing the shaft being rotated by hand.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the manufacturer's identification plate showing the model and year.
Video of the transmission being shifted through all gears to check for internal damage.
Photo of the output shaft to check for cracks.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
